assign.card: Framework home: grids without voids, layout labels

log.msg: the queued minion for this sub-task never cleared the Servex spawn gate (58+ min stuck, confirmed systemic; escalated to mastermind-servex-10). The parent task-mastermind did this work itself rather than wait indefinitely.

new file dev/DevBar/labels.js: a label pinned near every .grid/.masonry/.packed/.wall/.page-previews/.sprawl container, showing its classes, a glanceable layout summary ('grid - 4 cols - ~358px', or 'columns - N cols' for .masonry), and (owner addition, same day) the nearest ancestor with a real container-type + its container-name, or 'viewport' when none -- all three in ONE label, per the owner's own instruction.

toggle: a DevBar checkbox (tools.js 'page' tab, reused parts.js's check()/knob() pattern) AND ?layout=1 in the url -- both flip the SAME knob (settings.js), picked as the one source of truth so the checkbox and the url can never disagree. The overlay's mount/unmount watches the class via MutationObserver at module scope (not inside DevBar's tab-render tree), so ?layout=1 works even with the rail closed or never opened.

outermost-only de-dup bug found and fixed before shipping: the first version used el.closest(SELECTOR) to skip nested containers, which walked past .sprawl (several levels up, also in SELECTOR) and silently suppressed every section's own .packed label -- only .sprawl itself and one unrelated .grid got labelled (screenshot). Fixed to check the IMMEDIATE parent only (el.parentElement.matches(SELECTOR)); re-shot, every section now labelled correctly.

second bug found and fixed: a container inside a closed <details> (this page's own Readme section) has an all-zero getBoundingClientRect(), and the label pinned itself to the top-left corner on top of the sidebar's 'Framework' heading (screenshot). Fixed with el.checkVisibility() before placing a label -- re-shot, clean.

wired into tools.js's 'page' tab array (layoutLabels), CSS added to devbar.css under the existing dev-outline rule (color-scheme: dark, the rail's own tokens, pointer-events: none so a label never catches a click meant for the page under it).
proved: ?layout=1 screenshot at 1920 (headless) shows every section's own card-group container labelled, legible, non-overlapping, no stray labels -- see parent task.jsonl for the shot path.
